summary: Checked 62 claims against the codebase, found 6 mirages (0 critical, 1 major, 5 minor). Every file path, function name, column count, DiffIntvl value, ADR reference and CI-execution claim in the tech-spec is confirmed. The one substantive error is the '41 NewTestConnectVersion call sites' count (actual: 37 direct + 1 internal); the conclusion it supports — no caller changes behaviour — is independently confirmed correct.

findings.claim: tech-spec says: 'All 41 call sites pass written-out literals whose union is a subset of the map, so no caller changes behaviour' (Decision 5), repeated as '41 NewTestConnectVersion call sites verified' (Backward Compatibility / Consumer impact)
findings.reality: grep -ro 'NewTestConnectVersion' finds 40 textual occurrences: 3 in internal/postgres/testing.go (doc comment line 13, func declaration line 16, and one real call at line 10 inside NewTestConnect) and 37 in _test.go files spread over 23 files. Actual direct call sites = 37 (in 23 files), or 38 counting NewTestConnect's internal call — not 41 in 20 files. The source of the number, 012-...-code-research.md:719 ('41 call sites in 20 files'), contradicts its own enumeration on the next line, which sums to 37 across 23 files: activity 1, bgwriter 1, common 4, databases 2, functions 1, indexes 1, io 2, overview 4, pgcenter_schema 1, procpidstat 1, progress_analyze 1, progress_basebackup 1, progress_cluster 1, progress_copy 1, progress_create_index 1, progress_vacuum 1, replication 1, replication_slots 3, sizes 1, statements 5, tables 1, wal 1, stat/postgres 1.
findings.source: 012-feat-pg19-compatibility-baseline-tech-spec.md, Decision 5 (Rationale) and Backward Compatibility (Consumer impact); inherited from code-research.md:719
findings.fix: Replace '41 call sites' with '37 call sites in 23 test files (plus NewTestConnect's own call)' in both places. The substantive claim is verified independently and unchanged: the union of version values reaching the map is {90500, 90600, 100000..180000}, all present in the ports map (which also has an unused 90400), so removing the ports[140000] fallback changes the behaviour of zero existing callers.

findings.claim: tech-spec says: 'All 41 call sites pass written-out literals'
findings.reality: Every one of the 37 test call sites is literally `postgres.NewTestConnectVersion(version)` — a loop variable, not a written-out literal. The literals live one level up, in the `versions := []int{...}` / `overviewVersions` lists that drive the loops. The code-research states this correctly ('Each of them passes a loop variable drawn from one of the literal lists'); the tech-spec's compression loses the distinction.
findings.fix: Reword to 'All call sites pass a loop variable drawn from a written-out `[]int{...}` literal list; the union of those literals is a subset of the map.' The verified property (no computed or derived version anywhere in the tests) still holds.

findings.claim: tech-spec says: 'The 29 live-connection version loops gain 190000, so every existing query test executes against the PG 19 cluster' (Testing Strategy / Integration tests)
findings.reality: There are 37 `for _, version := range ...` loop statements that call NewTestConnectVersion, not 29. 29 is the number of distinct version-*list* edit points (code-research §B.1 table, 29 rows) — the discrepancy is that `internal/query/overview_test.go:13` (`overviewVersions`) feeds 4 loops and `internal/query/common_test.go:64` (`versions`) feeds 4 loops, so 8 loops collapse into 2 edits. 29 is the correct number of edits; it is not the number of loops.
findings.fix: Reword to 'The 29 live-connection version lists gain 190000 (covering 37 loops — overviewVersions and common_test.go's list each drive four)'. Also worth stating explicitly that `internal/query/databases_test.go:56` (`[]int{140000}`) and the three `internal/query/io_test.go` string-inspection loops at :68, :96, :179 are deliberately excluded, per code-research §B.2 — otherwise the sweep task has to re-derive that exclusion.

findings.claim: tech-spec says: 'the tests whose `t.Skipf` sits above the version loop (`common_test.go` x4, `overview_test.go` x4, `internal/stat/postgres_test.go`)' (Decision 7)
findings.reality: The set of nine tests is correct (common_test.go loops at :82, :99, :111, :125; overview_test.go at :18, :68, :128, :155; stat/postgres_test.go at :92), but in all nine the `t.Skipf` sits INSIDE the loop, immediately after `NewTestConnectVersion` — e.g. internal/stat/postgres_test.go:92-96 and internal/query/common_test.go:82-86. What actually distinguishes them from the well-formed tests is that the loop body is not wrapped in a per-version `t.Run(...)`, so `t.Skipf` fires on the parent `t` and aborts the whole test. Contrast internal/query/progress_vacuum_test.go:13-24, where the identical skip is inside `t.Run(fmt.Sprintf(...))` and skips one subtest only. The consequence the decision states is correct; the code-layout description is not.
findings.source: 012-feat-pg19-compatibility-baseline-tech-spec.md, Decision 7 (Decision + Rationale); inherited from code-research.md:835 ('skip is above the loop')
findings.fix: Reword to 'the tests whose `t.Skipf` fires on the parent `t` because the loop body is not wrapped in a per-version `t.Run`'. This also makes the tech-debt entry actionable — the fix is to add the subtest wrapper, not to move the skip.

findings.claim: acceptance criterion says: '`PostgresV19 = 190000` present; no other production file needs a new version branch'
findings.reality: Contradicted by the tech-spec's own Solution item 2 and Task 3, which add a `>= PostgresV19` branch to internal/query/progress_vacuum.go, progress_analyze.go and progress_basebackup.go, plus three new `case` blocks in internal/view/view.go:367-405. The Architecture bullet's phrasing ('The single seam; every version branch in the tree is an inequality with >= on the newest arm') is the accurate one and is fully confirmed: all existing production version comparisons are inequalities (bgwriter.go:42,46; wal.go:26; io.go:88; statements.go:335-337,348,357-359; activity.go:48-50; databases.go:47; replication.go:58; query.go:71; common.go:134-158; view.go:422; profile/profile.go:356; top/signal.go:86; internal/stat/log.go:109), and there is no equality comparison or switch on a version literal anywhere in production code.
findings.fix: Reword AC 1 to 'PostgresV19 = 190000 present; no EXISTING production version branch needs editing — every one is an inequality with >= on the newest arm, so 190000 lands on the newest arm by construction. The only new branches are the three progress selectors.'

findings.claim: Task 5 says: 'Describe the new columns in the three progress report descriptions' (position unspecified); Decision 1 fixes column placement to 'immediately before a.state — after relation on vacuum and analyze, after duration on basebackup'
findings.reality: report/describe.go's rows mirror the SELECT order one-for-one (pgStatProgressVacuumDescription at :202-220 lists pid, xact_age, datname, relation, state, waiting, phase, ... exactly matching the 13 query columns). The only place that names a describe.go insertion point is code-research.md:392 — 'Insert started_by / mode rows between datname (:207) and ...' — which is the superseded mid-interview placement Decision 1 explicitly retires. Task 5 neither restates Decision 1's placement nor lists the user-spec among its 'Files to read', so the row order in describe.go could end up not matching the query column order.
findings.source: 012-feat-pg19-compatibility-baseline-tech-spec.md, Task 5 (Description / Files to read); conflicting guidance at code-research.md:392-396
findings.fix: Add to Task 5: 'describe.go row order must mirror the query SELECT order per Decision 1 — started_by/mode after the relation row, backup_type after the duration row. Ignore code-research.md:392-396, which carries the superseded datname/pid placement.'
